dedupe_keys.name: minami ise japan environmental and economic evaluation of pre disaster plans for disaster waste management

description: This case study builds the methods and inventory data that municipalities need to judge the environmental and economic merits of their plans for handling waste after a future natural disaster, and applies them to the town of Minami-Ise in Mie prefecture, Japan. Tomohiro Tabata, Yohei Wakabayashi, Peii Tsai and Takashi Saeki of Kobe University and Toyama Prefectural University published it in Waste Management in 2017. They estimated about 554,000 tonnes of potential disaster waste from dwellings, needing about 55 hectares of temporary storage, and found that scarce local space would force transport to several other sites. Using life cycle assessment and life cycle costing, they evaluated scenarios for transporting, storing and recycling waste home appliances: carbon dioxide, sulphur oxide, nitrogen oxide and particulate emissions of 142 t, 7 kg, 257 kg and 38 kg, and a total cost of about 1.77 million US dollars. The article is available online, free to read on ScienceDirect. Caveats: the hazard scenario and inventory assumptions are specific to the town, and only four appliance types were costed in detail. Finishing all treatment in three years would meet the local sulphur oxide standard with 4.8 working hours a day at storage sites. Simulation uses: disaster waste quantities, storage land needs and process inventories for pre-disaster waste planning models. Related records: the Great East Japan earthquake disposal cost study (case_study-great-east-japan-earthquake-disaster-waste-disposal-cost-efficiency) analyses actual post-disaster costs.
